subject.title: Feature: Respect userTimezone in memory file timestamps and naming

question: Should bundled `session-memory` filenames and `# Session` headers use `agents.defaults.userTimezone` when it differs from the gateway host timezone?
rationale: Current docs and shipped behavior say host-local for session-memory, while memory-core compaction flush already uses configured userTimezone; changing the hook affects user-visible artifact naming and needs product approval.

options.title: Adopt userTimezone for session-memory
options.body: Make the hook follow the existing configured-user-timezone helper and align it with compaction flush behavior without adding a new config key.

options.title: Keep host-local session-memory
options.body: Close this as intentionally documented host-local behavior and leave only compaction flush on configured userTimezone.

options.title: Add a dedicated memory timezone knob
options.body: Introduce separate memory artifact timezone configuration, accepting extra config surface and migration/docs cost.

recommendation.title: Adopt userTimezone for session-memory
recommendation.body: Make the hook follow the existing configured-user-timezone helper and align it with compaction flush behavior without adding a new config key.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the current host-local session-memory behavior and are the strongest current-history owner for this specific hook semantics decision.
